subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, the tails fan up nicely and give a good silhouette from the front and back, with fine flame tips and ear tufts. The snout looks too thin and long and needs adjusting.

The cheek ruffs are oriented wrong — they stick forward as flat horizontal shards covering the eye and muzzle instead of flowing back and down like fur. I need to reorient the direction vector to point backward and down with a slight outward angle, and change the width vector so the blade forms a vertical side-facing plate rather than a horizontal plate crossing the face.

I'm also fixing the forehead fringe to sweep upward instead of jutting forward like a horn, shrinking the start positions so roots are buried properly in the head, and considering thickening the thin stilt-like legs since the body reads chunky with legs too thin by comparison.

Looking at other views: the lantern placement is fine (apparent clipping is just perspective), tails rising high in side view work and even blocking the fox from the rear is acceptable for a kitsune design, though the tail tuft spikes look a bit messy and the tails could be fluffier. The flame tips currently read as faceted crystal cones with seven segments — I could make them more flame-curved but might skip that refinement.

Checking the plinth: the pentagram inlay looks good, but the 3m plinth seems oversized relative to the 2.78m-wide fox, so I'm considering shrinking the octagon radius from 1.5 to 1.25 and pulling the lanterns and stones inward proportionally. The bigger issue is the tails extending back to around z=-1.48 while the plinth edge sits near z=-1.65, so they're close to overhanging — I could shift the plinth center back slightly or shorten the tails a touch to keep everything contained within the base.

Looking at the face now, the eyes are too small and get occluded by the cheek plate from the front angle, so I want to enlarge the eye decal size and shift its azimuth to around 42 degrees for better visibility. The muzzle is also too thin and long — I'm going to thicken the snout profile along its sweep path to give it a chunkier, more proportional look matching the jaw.

Checking the smaller details: whiskers, chest ruff, and dorsal spine blades look acceptable as-is. The tail tuft blades are too dark teal though, so I'll lighten their shadow tone using a flatter cel shading approach for better contrast against the body.

Now I'm reworking the cheek ruff geometry, adjusting the blade positions and directions for a thicker, more natural leg shape. Adjusting cheek blade parameters...

Next I'll update the leg radii sweeps and eye size values to resize the eyes and refine the fringe block, replacing the specific array values with new ones.

Adjusting eye azimuth, reworking the snout sweep to taper its radius along the profile, and updating the tail tuft color to use a shadow variant based on index parity.
